headline: 5,000 doctors to be recruited: BPSC issues 51st Special BCS circular
summary: The Bangladesh Public Service Commission has announced vacancies for 5,000 positions in the health cadre, including assistant surgeons and dental surgeons.
details: The Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC) has released the circular for the 51st Special BCS examination-2026.
The recruitment drive aims to fill 5,000 positions within the BCS (Health) cadre.
Of these vacancies, 4,700 posts are for assistant surgeons and 300 posts are for assistant dental surgeons.
Online applications for the examination will open on October 1 at 10:00 AM.
Interested candidates can apply online until October 25 at 6:00 PM.
caption:
5,000 doctors are being recruited for the 51st Special BCS! Applications open October 1.

The Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC) has released the circular for the 51st Special BCS examination-2026.

The recruitment drive aims to fill 5,000 positions within the BCS (Health) cadre.

Of these vacancies, 4,700 posts are for assistant surgeons and 300 posts are for assistant dental surgeons.

Online applications for the examination will open on October 1 at 10:00 AM.

Interested candidates can apply online until October 25 at 6:00 PM.

headline_marked: Govt to [[cut fuel prices if West Asia crisis eases]]
headline: Govt to cut fuel prices if West Asia crisis eases
summary: State Minister for Energy Aninda Islam Amit says the government will adjust domestic prices once global oil prices fall.
details: State Minister for Energy Aninda Islam Amit announced that the government will lower fuel prices if the crisis in West Asia eases and international oil prices drop.
Speaking in Meherpur on Thursday, Amit explained that the government had tried to absorb the higher costs for nearly six months before deciding to raise prices.
He stated that Bangladesh relies entirely on imported fuel as it does not produce petroleum domestically, making it vulnerable to global market fluctuations.
The Minister noted that war in the import region has disrupted global energy markets, pushing up prices in several countries.
Additionally, higher global oil prices, increased insurance premiums, and rising import costs have made it difficult for the government to avoid domestic price hikes.
caption:
Will fuel prices finally drop? The government says it depends on the West Asia crisis.

State Minister for Energy Aninda Islam Amit announced that the government will lower fuel prices if the crisis in West Asia eases and international oil prices drop.

Speaking in Meherpur on Thursday, Amit explained that the government had tried to absorb the higher costs for nearly six months before deciding to raise prices.

He stated that Bangladesh relies entirely on imported fuel as it does not produce petroleum domestically, making it vulnerable to global market fluctuations.

The Minister noted that war in the import region has disrupted global energy markets, pushing up prices in several countries.

Additionally, higher global oil prices, increased insurance premiums, and rising import costs have made it difficult for the government to avoid domestic price hikes.

#Bangladesh #FuelPrice #EnergyCrisis #Economy #GlobalOil

Source: bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV
